trajectory_summary: The call opens warm — a self-motivated returning-call customer who volunteers seasonal bill swings, a pool addition, and an existing Ion referral relationship largely unprompted. The rep runs the verify sequence efficiently and books a next-day appointment, but leaves the customer's stated travel-unavailability window unresolved against the booked date, and never pivots the bill-graph struggle to a faster verbal read-back despite repeated friction.

observed_outcome.quote: 05:00? K. Sounds good. K. Perfect. I have you on the schedule then for tomorrow, April 15 at 05:00 just for that phone call appointment with my specialist.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (tomorrow, April 15 at 5pm) was locked for a phone appointment; the wife was identified as co-title-holder at 01:07 but never explicitly invited onto the appointment call.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the $200/month average (plus seasonal swing to $300 in summer) but responded only with 'Jeez. That's crazy.' at 02:27 — a reaction, not a flip into alignment-against-the-utility. The flip should have gone right there, e.g. reframing that seasonal spike as the cost solar removes.

bill_document_audit.ask_quote: And so we just based that off your most recent electricity bill because on your electricity bill, there's a bar graph, and it shows the last twelve months of kilowatt usage.
bill_document_audit.result_quote: There you go. Now that's got the exact numbers on it.
bill_document_audit.reasoning: Rep explained the need for the bill graph, offered text or email, and the customer ultimately sent a usable screenshot with exact kWh numbers by the end of the call.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Now we were thinking about adding a pool, which is one of the reasons I wanna go with solar.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar' but the customer volunteered a reason (planned pool addition) mid-call; the rep logged it for notes but did not reinforce it verbally as leverage for sizing or urgency.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer switched utility providers only two days prior. The bill data captured later in the call (usage history, $7 bill from a 1-2 day billing cycle) reflects the OLD provider's account, not the new one — a data-quality issue for system design accuracy.

key_moments.stewart_read: A planned pool addition is a direct future-load enthusiasm signal — it will materially raise the customer's usage and strengthens the case for a larger system. The rep noted it for the file but didn't reflect it back as a reason solar makes even more sense now.

key_moments.stewart_read: A brief, reasonable sequencing answer to a logistics question, not a meaningful scope violation — the rep gave a light directional answer and immediately deferred detail to notes/specialist.

key_moments.stewart_read: Customer explicitly names his own tech friction. Schema's low-tech pivot calls for a fast move to verbal read-back within about two minutes; the rep instead persisted through photo/text channel-switching for several more minutes before the customer self-solved.
